# Spec axis review: pallets/click #3362, HEAD `20fff38`

## (c) Looks implemented, but the implementation looks wrong

**1. The fix probably does nothing. This is the most serious finding.**

> Spec: "expects the usage lines to contain intact options: `--max-retry-count --disable-cache-mode`"

The diff only adds a class attribute, `break_on_hyphens = False`, to `TextWrapper`. In CPython, `textwrap.TextWrapper.__init__` takes `break_on_hyphens=True` as a parameter and always sets `self.break_on_hyphens = break_on_hyphens` on the instance. That instance value hides the class value. `_split()` reads `self.break_on_hyphens` to choose between `wordsep_re` and `wordsep_simple_re`, so it will still see `True`.

The context shown (lines 38–55) has no `__init__` override in Click's subclass. The only call site, `formatting.py` lines 65–70, does not pass `break_on_hyphens=False`. So the output would most likely still split as `--max-` / `retry-count`, and the issue's reproduction would still fail.

I could not run anything, so this is based on reading the code and the standard library's behaviour. Two fixes would work:
- Pass `break_on_hyphens=False` at the call site.
- Override `__init__` in the subclass to set that default.

**2. No test covers the case in the issue.**

> Spec: "Its HelpFormatter(width=65) reproduction expects the usage lines…"

The diff adds no test using `HelpFormatter(width=65)` and the issue's options. A test like that would have caught finding 1 straight away. Since there is no test, nothing in the diff shows the requirement is met.

## (b) Scope creep

**3. The intended change reaches all help text, not just usage lines.**

> Spec: "The request concerns help usage wrapping, not all text formatting."

`TextWrapper` is used by `wrap_text()`, which formats more than usage lines. It also wraps command help, epilogs, option help in definition lists, and any other caller. If the attribute took effect, words like "well-known" or "command-line" in normal prose would no longer break at the hyphen anywhere.

The spec limits the request to usage wrapping. A narrower fix would turn off hyphen breaking only in the usage path, for example `write_usage` passing a flag through `wrap_text`. At the least, the wider change should be a deliberate, documented choice. Right now it is hidden in a class-level default.

## (a) Missing or partial

**4. The core requirement is not shown to be met.** Because of finding 1, the requirement is effectively missing: "the usage lines [should] contain intact options." There is also no changelog entry. That is minor, and it is not part of the spec itself.

## Summary

| # | Axis | Severity | Issue |
|---|------|----------|-------|
| 1 | (c) | High | The class attribute is overwritten by the instance attribute set in `__init__`, so the fix likely has no effect |
| 2 | (c)/(a) | Medium | No test reproduces the issue |
| 3 | (b) | Medium | The intended change affects all text wrapping, not just usage |
| 4 | (a) | Low | Requirement not shown to be met; no changelog entry |

No testing evidence was provided, on Windows or any other platform. Nothing was run for this review.
